Well, we have to start off with a classic, right?

They said it couldn't be done; that you couldn't teach the lower races about the true applications of science. But it was done, and it was done successfully. An industrial elvish metropolis sprawls in what was once a pristine and holy forest. The trees are long gone, and the shrines to the Gods now swallowed by concrete and steel.

It also wasn't done without sacrifice. Some of the early attempts to teach them science resulted in many ethical quandaries. How does one go about dealing with the issues that surround creating artificial centaurs by grafting orcs to horses? And what should one do if the graft does take? And furthermore, is it right to then breed those new centaurs in cramped industrial farms to help keep up with the growing demand for meat, leather, and a general elvish dislike for orcs? No matter, science must progress. And it did.

Industry now burgeons. The elves have given up their traditional ways of life, and are now consumed by the same capitalistic desire as we are. Their economies and their politics now form an eerie reflection of our own. In some ways it is as we desired, yet many men still feel a sort of sadness about that development. Some had hoped that they would have done better, or at the very least done something different. Or maybe this is just the natural progression of science, and whether you are man or elf, the progression will be the same.
